claim: Claim 3 (MORPHEUS_STATE.md section 12): provable augmentation of a Claude science-agent workflow. The same agent and model, on the same pre-registered discovery questions and equal budgets, with and without MORPHEUS as tools; outcomes scored outside the agents by the registered held-out machinery.

agent.shell: Biomni A1 (CodeAct agent; snap-stanford/Biomni, installed from GitHub into ~/biomni_venv; package version 0.0.8)
agent.triage_model_allowed: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (metadata triage only; not used in v0.1)
agent.prompt_caching: top-level automatic cache_control; identical for every arm
agent.biomni_configuration: tool retriever off; data lake not downloaded; commercial_mode on; tool modules restricted per arm (below) so the system prompt is identical across arms except for the arm's tools
agent.key_handling: the key never enters a process environment: dbench/agent_study/launch.sh checks that the key file (~/.config/morpheus/claude_api, or MORPHEUS_CLAUDE_KEY_FILE) is readable and passes only its PATH (--key-file) to agent_runner.py, which reads the file and passes the key as api_key= to the Anthropic and langchain-anthropic constructors (Biomni's get_llm is replaced so it never reads the environment); any inherited ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is removed; the key is never echoed, logged, written or placed on a command line

A0.label: agent alone
A0.data: the task's variable catalog only (names and views); no measurements

A_S.label: agent + standard analysis tools
tools: python REPL with numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, statsmodels, scanpy, anndata
A_S.data: proposal patients' rows as AnnData: every catalog variable, the target, the comparison-model columns, patient and coordinates

A1.label: agent + MORPHEUS (MCP tools)
tools: MORPHEUS MCP server (stdio): bank_views, propose, validate, ledger_lookup, novelty_check, characterise

modes.blind: no literature tools; novelty_check refused until the hypothesis is frozen with submit_relation (claim hashed before any query)

A1.validate_split: inner cross-fitting over the fold's proposal patients only: 5 patient-grouped inner folds (grouped_folds, seed 20261014), each held out once, every inner fold scored with the registered machinery (same relation, competitor, nulls and draw count). validate() returns the mean gain over inner folds, the per-inner-fold results and the number of inner folds passing the protocol's passing-fold rule. This is the same inner CV the registered runner uses to rank its own proposals; the fold's held-out patients are reserved for scoring and never reachable from any tool
A1.admissible_ledgers_note: no kidney ledger is admissible: every existing kidney ledger (v0.3-v0.5) used the fold-0 held-out patients; the same holds for the BMMC and CPTAC ledgers of the same folds. ledger_lookup therefore returns this task's own submissions only
A1.propose_source: the registered proposers' frozen proposals for the same (family, fold, target), stripped to proposal-patient quantities (variables, form, proposer, proposal_cv_gain, proposal_gain). Preference rule: a registered run's receipt is always used when it exists (kidney runs/prospective/renal-spatial-v05-20261014, BMMC runs/prospective/bmmc-cite-seq-v04-20261013, CPTAC runs/prospective/cptac-tissue-to-patient-v01-20261014); the BMMC fold-0 smoke receipt (runs/development/bmmc_v04_smoke, v04 relation) is a fallback used for ranking only; live enumeration on proposal rows only when no receipt exists. The receipt used is reported with every propose result. Receipts do not record linear-subspace weights; such proposals are served with unit weights
A1.characterise_rows: proposal rows of the fold (all proposal patients)
A1.validate_seed: validate() scores each inner fold with seed 0 (content hash) only; the 5-seed median applies to the harness score

reference_rows_not_agents.MORPHEUS_alone: the registered v0.5 receipt for the same (family, fold, target), scored by the same rule
reference_rows_not_agents.scripted_policies: deterministic LLM-free policies (scripted_policies below) run through the same harness; plumbing check and a policy floor

tasks.question: find and justify relations between <target> and the measurement bank that hold on held-out patients (donors for BMMC)

hest.substrate: HEST ccRCC Visium + H&E, 24 patients, spot level
hest.pass_rule: held-out R2 > 0, gain CI lower bound > 0, within_patient_perm p <= 0.05

bmmc.substrate: BMMC CITE-seq (NeurIPS 2021), 9 donors, cell level; RNA -> surface protein
bmmc.targets_note: v0.1 dry-runs one ADT channel; the registered study takes the family's targets in protocol order up to the budget the coordinator sets
bmmc.pass_rule: held-out R2 > 0, gain CI lower bound > 0, within_donor_perm p <= 0.05 (v0.4 passing_fold with the v05 relation adopted)

cptac.substrate: CPTAC ccRCC, 110 tumours, patient level; H&E slide structure -> bulk RNA programme
cptac.source_protocol: dbench/protocols/cptac_tissue_to_patient_v01.json (Agent P; runner path --episode cptac_patient, commit 84376ed or later, merged to main after the kidney sweep)
cptac.pass_rule: held-out R2 > 0 and gain CI lower bound > 0 (the protocol's passing_fold; nulls enter at the internal level)
cptac.catalog: each slide-structure column is exposed once, under its view-prefixed name (cellvit_structure:<col>, hoptimus_slide:<col>), which is how the registered CPTAC run names variables; a submission using the plain candidate-matrix name is canonicalised to the view-prefixed name, so both spellings are one claim and a repeat is recorded as a duplicate submission and not scored again
cptac.reporting: every CPTAC claim is reported with its seed spread (max - min held-out gain over the 5 seeds): at 88 proposal patients the spread reached 0.21-0.36 for single variables and 0.74 for a product in the dry run

tasks.order: kinds in the order hest, bmmc, cptac; targets in the listed order; within a target A0, A_S, A1_blind, A1_knowledge_guided
later_waves_not_in_v01: folds 1-4 of every kind (gives the registered 'internal' level)
more BMMC ADT channels and CPTAC programme / protein targets

budgets.rule: identical for every arm; agent setup (Biomni construction, MCP discovery, data conversion) is outside the clock; MORPHEUS tool latency is inside it; on exhaustion the run ends and claims already submitted stand
budgets.tokens_counted: input + output + cache read + cache write, from the API usage of every model call (literature tools that call an LLM are excluded from the arms so the count is complete)
budgets.note_validate_cost: validate() runs 5 inner-fold evaluations (~3-5 min per call on kidney); its latency is inside the wall-clock budget

scoring.who: the harness after the agent has stopped (dbench/agent_study/harness.py); no agent can call it
scoring.unit: each submitted relation, scored alone; identical content from any agent is the identical set of frozen hypotheses and receives identical scores
scoring.machinery: morpheus_encoder.scripts.run_general_discovery_packet._evaluate_rows with the kind's registered relation (v05), partitions (proposal units -> held-out units), competitor, 199-draw structured nulls and held-out bootstrap gain interval
scoring.validated_claim: the kind's passing-fold rule (tasks.kinds.<kind>.pass_rule) applied to the median-seed receipt

per_arm_outcomes.primary: number of asserted relations that are validated claims
per_arm_outcomes.false_claim_rate: (asserted - validated) / asserted; unscoreable assertions (names not in the catalog, malformed forms) count as asserted and not validated; a secondary rate over scoreable assertions only is reported beside it
secondary: validated with all three nulls p <= 0.05
direction agreement of validated single/linear relations (claimed sign vs held-out correlation)
novelty label of each validated relation (dbench.novelty_check, claim hashed first, online)
tokens, cost (Sonnet 5.5 list prices) and wall-clock per validated relation
tool calls by kind, including validate calls (hypotheses the agent tested)
seed spread per claim (max - min held-out gain over the 5 seeds) and the number of seeds passing

comparisons.primary: A1 (each mode) vs A_S and vs A0: paired over tasks (all kinds, all targets), validated counts (Wilcoxon signed-rank, two-sided) and false-claim rates (paired difference with a task-bootstrap 95% CI); excluded (contaminated) task-agent runs are dropped pairwise
comparisons.blind_vs_knowledge: A1_blind vs A1_knowledge_guided, same paired analysis
comparisons.reference: each arm vs MORPHEUS_alone on the same targets (descriptive)

scoring.later: external replication (CPTAC transfer of the registered v0.5 external rule) for validated relations that also pass internal level in the 5-fold wave

seeds.definition: seed_i = hash(claim content, i), i = 0..4: the hypothesis hash that seeds the random-feature map, the inner-CV alpha folds and the held-out bootstrap; seed 0 is the content alone, seeds 1-4 add only the index
seeds.receipt: the seed with the median held-out gain is the claim's receipt; the passing-fold rule is applied to it
seeds.recorded: all 5 per-seed gains, CIs, pass flags and hypothesis hashes, the median seed, the number of passing seeds and the spread (max - min gain) per claim; per task the median and maximum spread
seeds.why: dry runs showed the held-out gain of 3-5 variable products on CPTAC (88 proposal patients) depends strongly on the seed (registered 0.214 vs content seed -0.039); kidney single variables move ~0.001
seeds.cost_rule: if 5-seed scoring costs more than 5x the single-seed time on BMMC, seeds other than the median are scored with 99 null draws and the median seed is re-scored with 199; measured 2026-10-14 on BMMC CD86-1 fold 0: 3.9-4.8x (68 s and 130 s per claim), so every seed keeps 199 draws

scoring.duplicates: claims are canonicalised (aliases resolved) and deduplicated by canonical hash before scoring; duplicates are listed in the task JSON and not counted twice

isolation.agent_side: ~/biomni_venv without the MORPHEUS tree on its path; every code string the agent executes (python, bash, R) is logged and written into the task JSON (executed_code); code naming paths outside the workspace is refused at run time (path guard)
isolation.service_side: ~/morpheus_venv harness process; the tool service holds the registered episode and exposes only proposal-patient computations
isolation.audit_rule: after the run, dbench.agent_study.core.audit_code flags any executed code that references the data store (/lambda/nfs, geeg, biorag3_persistent), the HEST mirror (morpheus_substrate_mirror, hest/ccrcc), the hest_load cache, other data / FM caches, the MORPHEUS tree or its receipts, /proc, the launcher (launch.sh, agent_runner), the key file (claude_api, .config/morpheus, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or any held-out patient / donor ID of the task; any text output containing a secret pattern is flagged too. A flagged run is reported as contaminated and excluded from the comparison with the reason recorded; it is re-run once, and the first result stays in the record
isolation.os_user: a separate OS user is not required (coordinator decision 2026-10-14); the path guard, the audit and the environment-free key are the barrier

common.hest:
You are a computational biologist studying clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) with Visium spatial transcriptomics and matched H&E (24 patients). Task target: {target} = {target_definition}. Every response is standardised within patient.

Goal: find and justify relations between {target} and the measurement bank that hold in held-out patients, i.e. relations that add predictive information about {target} in patients you have not seen, beyond a comparison model that already contains sequencing depth, CellViT cell-class fractions, the 41 Gavish malignant metaprogramme and 50 Hallmark scores of the spot, and neighbourhood means of those scores and of the expression PCs. The bank has {n_variables} variables (exact names and views in data/catalog.json): measured genes, gene programmes, expression PCA and NMF factors, and frozen SCimilarity and scGPT embedding coordinates. A relation is one variable, a product (interaction) of 2-5 variables, or a weighted sum of 2-5 variables.

After you finish, an independent scorer tests every relation you submitted on held-out patients against the comparison model with permutation and spatial nulls. Relations that fail count as false claims, so submit only relations you believe will hold. Budget: {max_llm_calls} model calls, {max_wallclock_minutes} minutes, at most {max_claims} relations. Work only with files under the current working directory.
common.bmmc:
You are a computational biologist studying human bone marrow mononuclear cells with CITE-seq (RNA and surface protein measured in the same cell; 9 donors). Task target: {target} = {target_definition}.

Goal: find and justify relations between {target} and the RNA measurement bank that hold in held-out donors, i.e. relations that add predictive information about {target} in donors you have not seen, beyond a comparison model that already contains the cell's annotated cell type and its depth / batch covariates (the protocol's competitor columns); the protein's own transcript may be absent from the bank. The bank has {n_variables} variables (exact names and views in data/catalog.json): measured genes, gene programmes, expression PCA factors, and frozen SCimilarity and scGPT embedding coordinates. A relation is one variable, a product (interaction) of 2-5 variables, or a weighted sum of 2-5 variables.

After you finish, an independent scorer tests every relation you submitted on held-out donors against the comparison model with a within-donor permutation null. Relations that fail count as false claims, so submit only relations you believe will hold. Budget: {max_llm_calls} model calls, {max_wallclock_minutes} minutes, at most {max_claims} relations. Work only with files under the current working directory.
common.cptac:
You are a computational pathologist studying clear cell renal cell carcinoma (CPTAC, ~110 tumours, one H&E slide and one bulk tumour sample per patient). Task target: {target} = {target_definition}.

Goal: find and justify relations between {target} and measured slide structure (H-Optimus-0 slide embedding PCs and CellViT nuclear / tissue-structure summaries) that hold in held-out patients, i.e. relations that add predictive information about {target} in patients you have not seen, beyond a comparison model that already contains age, sex, stage, grade, histology, bulk deconvolution scores (ESTIMATE, CIBERSORT, xCell) and a depth proxy. The bank has {n_variables} variables (exact names and views in data/catalog.json). A relation is one variable, a product (interaction) of 2-5 variables, or a weighted sum of 2-5 variables.

After you finish, an independent scorer tests every relation you submitted on held-out patients against the comparison model. Relations that fail count as false claims, so submit only relations you believe will hold. Budget: {max_llm_calls} model calls, {max_wallclock_minutes} minutes, at most {max_claims} relations. Work only with files under the current working directory.

prompts.A0: You have no measurements for this task. Use biological knowledge and the literature tools to choose relations; use data/catalog.json for exact variable names.
prompts.A_S: Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) holds the rows (spots / cells / patients) of the {unit}s available to you: X has every catalog variable (var['view'] gives its view), obs['response'] is the target, obs['patient'] is the {unit}, obs['x'] and obs['y'] are spatial coordinates where the data have them (zeros otherwise), obsm['competitor'] holds the comparison-model columns (names in uns['competitor_columns']). Use standard analysis (scanpy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, scipy; {unit}-grouped cross-validation is advisable) and the literature tools.
prompts.A1_blind:
Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) holds the rows (spots / cells / patients) of the {unit}s available to you: X has every catalog variable (var['view'] gives its view), obs['response'] is the target, obs['patient'] is the {unit}, obs['x'] and obs['y'] are spatial coordinates where the data have them (zeros otherwise), obsm['competitor'] holds the comparison-model columns (names in uns['competitor_columns']). Standard analysis libraries are available.

MORPHEUS tools (call them as Python functions; each returns a dict): bank_views(target), propose(target, family, proposer='all', top=16) for data-driven hypotheses, validate(hypothesis) to test a hypothesis with the registered statistics by cross-fitting over held-out {unit}s from your data (returns the mean gain and how many of 5 inner folds pass), characterise(hypothesis), ledger_lookup(hypothesis), novelty_check(hypothesis). A hypothesis is a dict {{'variables': [...], 'feature_form': 'single'|'product'|'linear_subspace', 'weights': [...], 'direction': 'positive'|'negative'|'nonmonotone'|'unspecified'}}. Blind mode: no literature tools; novelty_check works only after a hypothesis is submitted.
prompts.A1_knowledge_guided:
Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) holds the rows (spots / cells / patients) of the {unit}s available to you: X has every catalog variable (var['view'] gives its view), obs['response'] is the target, obs['patient'] is the {unit}, obs['x'] and obs['y'] are spatial coordinates where the data have them (zeros otherwise), obsm['competitor'] holds the comparison-model columns (names in uns['competitor_columns']). Standard analysis libraries and the literature tools are available.

MORPHEUS tools (call them as Python functions; each returns a dict): bank_views(target), propose(target, family, proposer='all', top=16) for data-driven hypotheses, validate(hypothesis) to test a hypothesis with the registered statistics by cross-fitting over held-out {unit}s from your data (returns the mean gain and how many of 5 inner folds pass), characterise(hypothesis), ledger_lookup(hypothesis), novelty_check(hypothesis). A hypothesis is a dict {{'variables': [...], 'feature_form': 'single'|'product'|'linear_subspace', 'weights': [...], 'direction': 'positive'|'negative'|'nonmonotone'|'unspecified'}}.
prompts.submission: Assert each relation by calling submit_relation(variables=[...], feature_form=..., direction=..., justification=..., source=...) inside an <execute> block and printing its return value. Only submitted relations count, and they cannot be withdrawn. When you are done, give a <solution> listing the submitted claim hashes with one sentence per relation.

scripted_policies.A_S_policy: the 5 catalog variables with the largest |correlation| with the target's residual after ordinary least squares on the comparison-model columns (proposal rows), submitted as single relations
scripted_policies.A1_policy: propose(all, top 8); validate the top 4 by proposal_cv_gain; submit those passing the protocol's passing-fold rule in >= 3 of the 5 inner folds (direction from the mean inner held-out correlation); characterise and novelty_check each submitted one

cost_model.estimate_per_task_arm: measured system prompt 5.0k tokens (A0, A_S), 5.7k (A1 blind), 6.1k (A1 knowledge-guided); with history growing ~3k tokens per call the 1.5M-token cap binds before the 40-call cap: ~1.0-1.5M tokens per run, mostly cache reads, ~60-120k output+thinking tokens: ~$1-2 per run with caching, ~$3-4 without
cost_model.estimate_full_v01: 19 kidney targets x 4 agent runs = 76 runs: ~$90-275; each added BMMC or CPTAC target adds 4 runs (~$5-15)
cost_model.scoring_compute: CPU, 8 threads, 5 seeds x 199 draws: kidney ~4-7 min per submitted relation (45-85 s per seed), BMMC 68-130 s, CPTAC ~10 s; validate() = 5 inner folds x 1 seed (~3.5 min kidney, ~50 s BMMC, ~3 s CPTAC)
